Smt. Sandhya Kabra vs Housing And Environment Department
on 8 October, 2025
Author: Pranay Verma

Bench: Pranay Verma
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:29404
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pranay Verma
 On The 8 th Of October, 2025
 Writ Petition No. 12447 of 2019
 Smt. Sandhya Kabra And Others
 Versus
 Housing And Environment Department And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Abhishek Gilke - Advocate for the petitioners.

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Kushal Goyal - Dy. A.G. for the respondents/State
 Shri Bharat Yadav - Advocate for the respondent No.2.
 Order

By this petition preferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioners have prayed for the following reliefs:-
"A. Grant the developed plot to the petitioner in scheme no.140 developed by Indore development authority with all consequential benefits. B. Any other writ, direction or order that the justice of this case may require."
02.

An objection has been taken by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 as regards maintainability of this petition on the ground that the petitioners have already resorted to the remedy of a reference for seeking enhancement of amount of compensation hence this parallel proceeding is not maintainable.

03. The land of the petitioners bearing Survey No.572/8 area 0.112 hectare Pipliyahana, Patwari Halka No.40, Tehsil and District Indore was included in Scheme No.140 of the Indore Development Authority (IDA), NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29404 2 WP-12447-2019 respondent No.2.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority (IDA), NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The land was acquired by the respondents and the acquisition proceedings were completed and award was passed.

Thereafter, the petitioners filed a reference before the Civil Court for Smt. Sandhya Kabra vs Housing And Environment Department on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12102715/
1 enhancement of the amount of compensation and also approached the respondents for grant of 20%
developed plot to him under the M.P. Awas Niti, 1995.

entities.text: Smt. Sandhya Kabra vs Housing And Environment Department
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 04. Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that both the aforesaid remedies simultaneously could have very well been resorted to by the petitioners.
Only for the reason that they resorted to the remedy of challenging the amount of compensation by approaching the Civil Court, they cannot be denied the plot to them as per the policy.
In any case, the petitioners have not received the amount of compensation as determined under the award.
The present petition is hence very much maintainable.
05. The land of the petitioners was acquired and an award in that regard was passed by the Land Acquisition Officer on 06.08.2005.
On 09.09.2005, a representation was given by the petitioners to the respondents for allotment of 20% developed plot to them.

However, without waiting for any decision on the said representation, on 04.10.2005 a reference was filed by the petitioners by way of an application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 before the Collector.
The matter was referred to the Civil Court and eventually by award dated 14.10.2015, the reference was dismissed.
In the meanwhile, a Writ Petition had been preferred by the petitioners which was decided on 12.10.2011.

Thereafter, the present petition was filed on 26.06.2019.
06.

Under the M.P. Awas Niti, 1995, the petitioners had a right either NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29404 3 WP-12447-2019 to claim 20% of developed plot in lieu of their acquired land or they could have received the amount of compensation as determined for the same.
Both the remedies are exclusive and in the alternate and could not have been resorted to simultaneously.
Only one remedy could have been chosen.
The petitioners cannot contend that they can claim enhancement of the amount of compensation and can simultaneously claim allotment of 20% of developed plots.
They had the choice of exercising either of the options.

The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that both the remedies can be resorted to by the petitioners simultaneously and benefits under both of them can be received is not acceptable.
07. Though the petitioners had filed representation on 09.09.2005 for allotment of developed plot but immediately thereafter also filed a reference which has eventually been decided on 14.10.2015.

Admittedly, against the same, no appeal has been preferred by the petitioners hence the same has attained finality meaning thereby that for acquisition of their land one of the remedy to which they were entitled has already been exhausted by them.
Consequently, it is not permissible for them to resort to the other remedy i.e. for allotment of plot as has been sought by them in this petition.

Pertinently, this petition has been preferred after decision of the reference without any challenge to the same and after a period of four years hence the petition also suffers from unexplained delay and latches.
In effect the petitioners are trying to seek modification of the award passed in the reference case which is impermissible.

08. Thus, in view of the decision of the reference of the petitioners by NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29404 4 WP-12447-2019 award dated 14.10.2015, the relief as claimed for by them cannot be granted.
The petition is consequently found to be not maintainable and is accordingly dismissed as such.
